title: The Valley of the Kings
objective: After this level you can explain why pharaohs chose a hidden valley for their tombs.
summary: From Thutmose I, New Kingdom kings hid rock-cut tombs in a desert valley at Thebes under a pyramid-shaped peak, with temples built apart. Almost all were robbed anyway.

cards.headline: Pyramids told everyone where a king was buried. That was the problem.
cards.body: New Kingdom pharaohs, fearing for their rich burials, tried another plan: hide the tomb, and hope nobody finds it.

cards.headline: A lonely valley
cards.body: Thutmose I is thought to have been the first king to cut his tomb in the Valley of the Kings, a narrow valley in the western hills at Thebes, probably for security. Kings of the 18th, 19th and 20th Dynasties followed, hiding their rock-cut tombs out of sight. Remember Level 3’s red land? Its dry climate made the desert an ideal place for cemeteries.

cards.headline: A pyramid after all
cards.body: Pharaohs didn’t give up on pyramids entirely. Above the valley rises a peak called the Qurn, whose shape may have reminded Egyptians of a pyramid. Their temples for worship after death were built separately, at the edge of the farmland, far from the hidden tombs. The tomb went into hiding; the temple stayed on show.

cards.headline: Built to baffle
cards.body: A typical tomb was a corridor sloping down into the rock, broken by deep shafts (perhaps to stop robbers, perhaps to catch floodwater), ending in a burial chamber. It didn’t work. Virtually every tomb in the valley was emptied in ancient times; Tutankhamun’s is the famous one that escaped. Hidden, it turns out, isn’t the same as safe.

mascot.line: This finishes Level 29’s lesson: a tomb everyone can see gets found. Hidden wasn’t safe either.

cards.headline: The valley: explored
learned: From Thutmose I, kings hid rock-cut tombs at Thebes
The Qurn peak stood in for a pyramid
Mortuary temples were built apart, by the farmland
Almost every tomb was robbed anyway

questions.prompt: Which king is thought to have been the first to cut his tomb in the Valley of the Kings?

options.label: Ahmose
options.rationale: The valley’s first royal tomb came a little later.

options.label: Narmer
options.rationale: He lived long before the New Kingdom.

options.label: Kamose
options.rationale: He fought the Hyksos; the valley’s first tomb was someone else’s.

questions.explanation: Thutmose I is thought to have been the first king buried in the valley, probably for security.

questions.prompt: Why did New Kingdom kings hide their tombs in a remote valley?

options.label: Priests had banned the building of pyramids
options.rationale: The reason was security, not a ban.

options.label: To protect their rich burials from robbers
To be closer to the Nile’s yearly flood
options.rationale: The valley is dry desert, away from the flood.

options.label: Because the valley was sacred to the Aten
options.rationale: The Aten had nothing to do with it.

questions.explanation: Fearing for their rich burials, kings hid rock-cut tombs out of sight, though almost all were robbed anyway.

questions.prompt: The Valley of the Kings lies in the desert hills. From Level 3, what made the red land a good place for burials?

options.label: Its rich black soil
options.rationale: That was the black land, used for farming.

options.label: Its closeness to the sea
options.rationale: The valley is far inland at Thebes.

questions.explanation: The desert’s dry climate made it an ideal place for cemeteries.
